clue.text: Agree map at sea would show strength of current

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cartographer's quip that a map of agreement would reveal how strong an ocean current runs.
explanation.definitionFit: Amperage is the size of an electric current measured in amps, its strength.

clue.text: Desperate model, extremely small

parts.note: a last is a shoemaker's wooden model of a foot
minute (my-NEWT) means tiny

explanation.surface: A fashion model in a frantic state, and very tiny too.
explanation.walkthrough: The cobbler's last is the less familiar sense of 'model' here, not a catwalk model.
explanation.definitionFit: A last-minute effort is a frantic, desperate one made when time has almost run out.

clue.text: See 24
Ministers persist in a stupid way

indicators.note: doing something stupidly suggests disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Government ministers stubbornly keep at something foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Ministers' sound like politicians; here they are ministers of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Priests are clergy, and a minister is a member of the clergy who serves a congregation.

clue.text: See 10
Compliance in underwater action?

parts.note: short for submarine, an underwater vessel
a mission is an operation or action undertaken

explanation.surface: Asking whether obedience is shown in some underwater operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the punning split of the answer into a submarine's mission.
explanation.definitionFit: Submission is the act of yielding or obeying, which is compliance.

clue.text: Sounds like children's author demanded money

indicators.note: says the answer is spoken the same as the author's name

parts.note: Arthur Ransome, who wrote Swallows and Amazons

explanation.surface: A writer of children's books apparently asked to be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons; his surname sounds the same as the answer once the final E is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A ransom is a sum of money demanded for releasing a captive.

clue.text: One member to broadcast, with little hesitation to be a wrecker

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament
to air a programme is to broadcast it
er is a short hesitating sound

explanation.surface: A politician who goes on air and, hardly hesitating, turns out to be a destroyer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impairs things damages or spoils them, so it is a wrecker.

clue.text: President — genuine fellow but spurned English

indicators.note: spurning something rejects it, so this letter is thrown out

parts.note: true means genuine
a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A president described as an authentic chap who rejected the English.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE + MAN loses its E (English) to leave the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry S. Truman was the 33rd President of the United States.

clue.text: Socialist up for election hopelessly outperformed

parts.note: socialists are on the political left
a candidate who is standing is running for office

explanation.surface: A socialist candidate in an election who was thoroughly beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To be left standing is an idiom for being so far outpaced by rivals that you seem not to have moved.

clue.text: Me — native abroad to the south-east

definitions.text: Me — native abroad to the south-east

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered, so these letters are spread about and reordered

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east

explanation.surface: A speaker introduces themselves as a native of a land far off to the south-east.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a person from Vietnam, in South-East Asia, speaking of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vietnamese person is a native of Vietnam, a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Runs? Opening bat will miss a century, I'll say!

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: missing something means leaving it out, so those letters go

parts.note: Mike Atherton, a former England opening batsman
a ton is a hundred, a century in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricket exclamation: the opener falls short of a hundred runs, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: Mike Atherton opened the batting for England; drop TON, cricket slang for a century, and put R in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rather! is a dated British exclamation of emphatic agreement, like saying 'definitely'.

clue.text: Bikers take risks ignoring them — hairy types!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what cyclists steer by, and riding no-hands means ignoring them
second meaning: moustaches curled up at the ends, like a bicycle's bars

explanation.walkthrough: The first half pictures a cyclist riding no-hands; the second is a style of facial hair named after the bicycle part.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the steering bar of a bicycle and a wide moustache with upturned ends.

clue.text: Demanding book should include paintings

indicators.note: including something puts it inside, so the paintings go into the book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
oils are oil paintings

explanation.surface: A difficult volume that ought to contain artworks.
explanation.definitionFit: Toilsome work requires hard labour, so it is demanding.

clue.text: A number sitting in boozy US diner?

indicators.note: sitting in something means being placed inside it

parts.note: beery means smelling of or fond of beer
N is the mathematical symbol for a number

explanation.surface: Someone counting customers in a drunken American eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanery is American slang for a cheap restaurant, a diner serving simple food like beans.

clue.text: Dress at about one for Italian food

parts.note: rig is to dress or kit out
on means about or concerning
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Instructions to get dressed around one o'clock for an Italian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a kind of ridged tubular pasta, an Italian staple.

clue.text: Silly editing gets one fired up

indicators.note: silly suggests the letters behave foolishly and get jumbled

explanation.surface: Foolish editing makes someone angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignited means set alight, literally fired up, and figuratively roused or excited.

clue.text: Gets aboard vehicle, being outside school

indicators.note: the first word sits around the second, so it goes outside it

parts.note: ens is a philosophical term for a being or entity
to school is to train or teach

explanation.surface: Someone boards a bus while standing outside a school.
explanation.walkthrough: ENS is a philosophers' Latin term for an entity; 'Gets aboard vehicle' is the definition, so 'school' must be the verb meaning train.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train, which is getting aboard a particular vehicle.

clue.text: Pope found in English river — a kind of fish

indicators.note: being found in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England, famous for trout
Leo is the name of many popes

explanation.surface: A pope turns up in an English river and turns out to be a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Teleosts are the bony fishes, the largest group of fish species.

clue.text: Final message poet composed with guile — waste of time!

indicators.note: composing arranges things anew, so these letters are reordered
wasting something means losing it, so this letter is dropped from the mix

explanation.surface: A poet's closing words, written cunningly, were a pointless use of time.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix the letters of POET and GUILE, which contain one T more than the answer; wasting that T leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An epilogue is a concluding section or speech at the end of a book or play.

clue.text: Piggy is middle character of three in game

indicators.note: the letter is put inside the card game

parts.note: poker is a card game

indicators.note: picks the centre letter of the word three

explanation.surface: Someone called Piggy is playing a card game in a threesome.
explanation.definitionFit: A porker is a pig fattened for pork, and Piggy is a nursery name for a pig.

clue.text: See 2
Glove making hit but missing the head

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is lost

parts.note: smitten is a past form of smite, to hit

explanation.surface: Glove-making struck someone, but they kept their head out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mitten is a glove with one section for all four fingers.

clue.text: Literary world to stroke good person in welcome

indicators.note: puts the pieces inside the welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
to rub is to stroke
St is a saint, a good person

explanation.surface: Literary types like to pet a decent chap when greeting him.
explanation.walkthrough: St, short for saint, is the crossword's usual 'good person'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grub Street was a London street of hack writers, and the name now stands for the world of jobbing literary work.

clue.text: See 26
Machine's very good — was first to get running water

parts.note: pi is slang for pious, very good
led means was in front
a river is a body of flowing water

explanation.surface: A device is excellent at being first to reach flowing water.
explanation.walkthrough: PI, short for pious, is a crossword favourite for 'very good'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile-driver is a machine that hammers posts into the ground for foundations.

clue.text: Slowly pass present back to grab attention

indicators.note: grabbing takes something into its grip, so the attention goes inside
back means the word is read the other way

parts.note: now is the present time
to have someone's ear is to have their attention

explanation.surface: Handing a gift back to someone in order to catch their notice.
explanation.definitionFit: When time wears on, it passes slowly and tediously.

clue.text: Angel's help is unexpectedly making a task very easy

indicators.note: something that happens unexpectedly comes out in a surprising order

explanation.surface: Help from an angel turns a job into child's play.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Like shelling peas' is a British idiom for a job that is simple to do.
